newsitem.title: USA: U.S. natural gas pipeline explodes.
newsitem.headline: U.S. natural gas pipeline explodes.

text.p: A natural gas pipeline broke in southern Washington state on Sunday, causing an explosion and sending a huge fireball into the air, officials said.

The explosion, near the small town of Kalama, was the second natural gas pipeline blast in Washington state in two days. A similar explosion and fire was reported on Saturday night near Bellingham, 70 miles (110 kms) north of Seattle.
Both explosions, about 200 miles (320 kms) apart, were on the same pipeline operated by Northwest Pipeline Corp, based in Salt Lake City, Utah, the company said.

"It's unusual to have one break. It's extremely unusual to have two," company spokesman John Nicksich said. The cause of the breaks was under investigation, but they did not appear to be related, he said.

The 26-inch (66 cm) diameter high pressure natural gas pipeline broke and exploded on Sunday evening, sending flames at least 100 feet (30 metres) into the air, Ray Byers, a spokesman for Cowlitz County Emergency Management, said.
Crews shut off valves, cutting off natural gas supply to that section of the pipeline, and let the remaining gas burn itself out, he said.
Between 50 and 75 people were evacuated from nearby homes as a precaution, Byers said.

The explosion happened in a timber area about 30 miles (50 kms) north of Portland, Oregon, that is sparsely populated and no one was injured, Byers said. No buildings were damaged but the blaze burned an area of timber about 100 yards (metres) in diameter, he said.

On Saturday night, the same 26-inch pipeline ruptured in a sparsely-populated area near Bellingham, at the opposite end of Washington state. Neil Clement, deputy director of Whatcom County Division of Emergency Management, said there were no injuries and damage appeared limited to the pipeline.

Nicksich said that, after both pipeline breaks, the company was able to switch customers over to another 30-inch natural gas pipeline that runs parallel to the affected line. The company did not expect any disruption in service to its customers in the Pacific Northwest.

Northwest Pipeline operates a 4,000-mile (6,400-km) high pressure natural gas transmission system that originates in the San Juan Basin in northwestern New Mexico and extends to the U.S.-Canadian border.
The pipeline carries natural gas from Canada, Wyoming, Utah and New Mexico and supplies it to customers in Washington state, Oregon and Idaho, Nicksich said.
Nicksich said it would be Monday evening at the earliest before the section of pipeline damaged in Saturday's explosion could be repaired and back in operation.
